fields.kind: realm, city-state, tribe, order, cult, company, criminal, court or plane
fields.tier: the faction's reach on the shared ladder
fields.clock_seeds: starting clocks for Milestone 2's faction clocks: what they are racing toward and how many segments
fields.eras: campaign eras the entry applies to; missing means all three

factions.name: The Kingdom of Cyrel
factions.summary: A stubborn fortress kingdom of three sister cities, fighting on two fronts and logging a third.
goals: Beat Asania, or at least not lose
Cut the timber the war needs

factions.name: The Kingdom of Asania
factions.summary: Splendid, magical, land-hungry and always ready for war. Allied with Trein's sorcerers, careful around Wrenspire.
goals: Stay first among the Kingdoms of Man

factions.name: The Lamplighters' Council of Trein
factions.summary: Trein is governed by the Lamplighters' Council, named for the old duty of keeping the city's Ley-lamps lit. Seven seats: four great mage houses, two merchant houses, and the Guild of Wardwrights who keep the city's wards running. A Lord-Speaker chosen by the seven chairs it. Every seat depends on crystal, so crystal policy is all the council really argues about.
goals: Post-Reform: decide whether to bring back casting licences

by_era.brotherhood: Still sits, but in practice rubber-stamps the Brotherhood of Man.
by_era.post-reform: House Orme carries the licence motion, with money nobody can trace (it is Mistress Sara's).

factions.origin_note: Trein is source; its council is a draft.

factions.name: The Brotherhood of Man
factions.summary: Publicly, a secular movement for mortal self-rule: magic for mortals, no more divine leash. In truth the instrument of Mistress Sara, the Eternal White Dragon Saradrosk, who wants the Ley under her control.
goals: Find where the New Gods hid the Font (Post-Reform)
assets: a research wing, a policy wing and a licensing wing

by_era.pre-reform: Not yet founded (2984). Sara cultivates the people who will found it.
by_era.brotherhood: Rules magic openly from Trein; the Dam stands.
by_era.post-reform: Officially gone for centuries. Secretly revived by Sara, its first rising in centuries, with small cells and a licence campaign in Trein's council.

factions.name: The Wrenspire Council
factions.summary: A high-minded council of engineers running a city that refuses magic, building ships and airships with gears alone.
goals: Stay independent of Trein and Asania

factions.name: The Stoneheart Clan
factions.summary: The blue-eyed ruling clan of the Dwarven Empire, descended from Dun Aldun's founders. Fair, hard, and patient through every winter.
goals: Hold the Rulan Gaan cult in check
Profit from the world's need for steel

factions.name: The Cult of Vymnommyth
factions.summary: Dwarves who broke from the Empire to worship the Eternal black dragon of Rulan Gaan as a god of rot and renewal, protection through contamination. What preserves you is what poisons you.
goals: Make the world around it hostile

clock_seeds.name: The swamp reaches the Dun Aldun road

factions.name: Master Grimm's workshop
factions.summary: The smithy behind most of the world's enchanted weapons and armor. Its master is the Eternal green dragon Forgrimmorithal.

factions.name: The Mossrun Expedition
factions.summary: A mining concern grown over five generations from two strikes, one iron and one Ley crystal, into an empire of mines serving several cities. Run by the Ilvar family, whose wives die in childbirth and whose fathers are always dying when the children come home.

clock_seeds.name: The Deep Nine reaches what it is digging toward

factions.name: The Cyrel Timber Guild
factions.summary: The guild that owns Kingswood's cutting crews and most of its debts. It has bought the Heartwood cutting rights from the town's reeve, in secret.
goals: Fell the Heartwood before the season ends

factions.name: The Unguruk Tribe
factions.summary: Orcs, half-orcs and human exiles in a walled camp at the heart of the Badlands. Proud, tough, and nursing a long grudge against Cyrel.

factions.name: The Dramogon Tribe
factions.summary: Gnoll-majority nomads of the northern Badlands under the shadow of Haggoth, the Gnoll Lord. Stoic, relentless, silent and everywhere.

factions.name: The Kadragar Tribe
factions.summary: Goblin seafarers, merchants and warriors of the southern Badlands coast, running the trade routes to Ota'at. Their god king is the Erlking.
goals: Control of the southern sea lanes
methods: negotiation with a knife behind it

factions.name: The High Elves of Brynwyr
factions.summary: A closed, ancient people defending their forest from Cyrel and its loggers, with wardens on the land and sea-elves on the water.

factions.name: The Wood Elves of Petrakyra
factions.summary: A reclusive people who trade sparingly with Obirykan and talk only to the Benzaiten monks. An Eternal Dragon is rumored to live among them.

factions.name: The Obirykan City States
factions.summary: Plutocrats who measure everything in Ley crystal. Each state fights to control the wealth and flow of Ley.
goals: Own more crystal than the next state

factions.name: The Dreadfall Corsairs
factions.summary: The pirates of the Scullcrossed Islands. Cruel, rarely survived, and always one ship ahead in the Gulf's arms race.

factions.name: The Benzaiten Monastery
factions.summary: Monks of many peoples on Ikto Isle, training mind and body, resolving conflict quietly. The only outsiders the wood elves of Petrakyra talk to.

factions.name: The Fjallagracht clans
factions.summary: Three clans hold the frozen island and its sea: Clan Skarth, raiders and fighters; Clan Hvalborg, whalers and longship-builders; and Clan Rimvik, the stone-keepers who read the Gurdalur calendar and so decide when anyone may sail, marry, bury or raid. Rimvik is the smallest clan and the one the others obey.
goals: Raid the mainland when the calendar allows
factions.origin_note: The island and the stones are source; the clans as a faction are a draft.

clans.name: Clan Skarth
clans.note: Raiders; the mainland's idea of Fjallagracht.

clans.name: Clan Hvalborg
clans.note: Whalers and shipwrights; they know the Dire Sea's summer windows.

factions.name: The Seelie Court
factions.summary: Titania's summer court of light, art and wild growth.

factions.name: The Unseelie Court
factions.summary: Mab's winter court of cold, shadow and the decay that feeds rebirth. Meddles in mortal affairs.

factions.name: The Nine Hells
factions.summary: The archdevils and their courts. On the Material Plane they work through contracts and cults.
goals: Post-Reform: recover the eight pieces of Asmodeus

fronts.name: Mammon's cults
fronts.note: Economic sabotage against prosperous states, through mortal fronts.

fronts.name: The Hellfire cult
fronts.note: Mephistopheles offers mortals the mastery of hellfire to grow his following.

fronts.name: Naamah's eyes
fronts.note: Spies and fledgling cults gathering leverage for her father's favor.

fronts.name: Lilith's followers
fronts.note: A large mortal following that answers to Lilith first and Beelzebub second.

factions.name: The Abyss
factions.summary: The demon lords. They do not recruit so much as devour; their mortal followers are the Dramogon gnolls' god-hunger, Orcus's necromancers and Belphegor's indulgent courts.
